status: DRAFT for review (Batch 4). Maps USDA FDC NAMES (plus record attributes) of 'Cereal Grains and Pasta' to candidate lexicon rows: PLAIN GRAINS (kind whole_food) and PLAIN FLOURS/MEALS (kind flour). Pasta, noodles, breakfast cereals, enriched/fortified/bleached forms, starches, bran/germ fractions and processed products are NOT this batch. FDC supplies naming evidence only; placement comes from the FAO clauses.
form_phrase: plain grain or plain flour form

clause.text: grains such as brown, parboiled or white rice, corn cob or kernel, wheat berry or grain
clause.where: FAO 2019 (Monteiro et al.), Table 1, Group 1 examples, p. 11
clause.basis: inference level: class-instance of grains; the clause names rice (brown, parboiled, white), corn cob or kernel and wheat berry or grain; other cereals and pseudo-cereals (oats, barley, millets, sorghum, quinoa, buckwheat, rye) are instances of the class 'grains', not named
clause.scope: The clause is unconditioned. A plain whole grain or a plain flour of it is an instance (flour: the next clause). Pasta, noodles, breakfast cereals, bread, starches, bran/germ fractions, enriched/fortified/bleached forms, pre-gelatinized or nixtamalized products, canned or cooked forms and mixes are not accepted here.

clauses_alt.text: grits, flakes or flour made from corn, wheat, oats, or cassava
clauses_alt.where: FAO 2019, Table 1, Group 1 examples (minimally processed), p. 11
clauses_alt.basis: inference level: class-instance of grits/flour; the clause names flour of corn, wheat, oats and cassava; flours of rice, rye, barley, millet, sorghum, buckwheat, quinoa, amaranth are instances of 'flour made from ... grains' (not named)

acceptance: A1. The FDC food category is exactly 'Cereal Grains and Pasta'.
A2. The plain form is established by the name ('raw', 'dry', 'whole grain', a flour/meal entry) or by a Foundation FoodOn '(raw)' attribute.
A3. No word from the word guard, product word or queue word.
A4. Record attributes do not contradict the plain form.
A5. The derived label term is a distinct food name: else QUEUE.
A6. Canonical deduplication: variety, grade (dark/light/medium, hard/soft, red/white), grain-length and cut variants collapse into ONE row; others are synonym CANDIDATES (synonyms.csv untouched).

word_guard.why: The category-wide extension of the Spices and Herbs word guard (owner rule 3). 'parboiled' is NOT guarded (the clause names parboiled rice); 'roasted' and 'toasted' are guarded AT STAGING only (the FDC grain clauses G1/G2 do not mention them). ALIGNED with runtime (per-form-1, owner ruling): the FAO p.6 methods clause names ROASTING, so plain roasted/toasted whole_food and flour items are Group 1 at runtime ('toasted' is an inference from roasting); a staging row for an FDC roasted record would be accepted by a later batch on that basis; 'unenriched' and 'unbleached' are plain-form words (not guarded).

product_words.why: A pasta, noodle, cereal, bread, starch, gluten, pre-gelatinized, nixtamalized (hominy, masa), degermed, enriched, fortified or bleached item is a product, a fraction or a treated form, not the plain grain or flour: REJECT. 'enriched/fortified/bleached' forms follow the owner's pending per-form decision (process-terms review P-C); 'bran'/'germ' are milling fractions.

queue_words.sprouted: sprouted grains: process-terms review proposes per-term inference rows from the general method clause; owner decision pending (P-A).
queue_words.wheat gluten: gluten is a FAO Group 4 substance.
queue_words.arrowroot: arrowroot flour is a starch product (FAO Group 2 starch example), not a grain flour.
queue_words.00: a flour grade name; no label word established.
queue_words.kernza: a trademarked perennial wheatgrass grain; rare; QUEUE.
queue_words.pearled: pearled grains are polished (a milling step beyond the clause's whole grain); QUEUE per-term.
queue_words.bulgur: parboiled cracked wheat: the clause names 'parboiled' rice; per-term decision.
queue_words.couscous: couscous is named in the Group 1 DEFINITION ('pasta, couscous and polenta made with flours, flakes or grits and water'), not in the examples: per-term decision.
queue_words.rolled: rolled oats are flaked (process); the clause names 'flakes' of oats: per-term decision (existing 'oat' row).
queue_words.corn: corn overlaps vegetables (sweet corn, queued in Batch 2) and cereal; QUEUE for an owner decision on corn.
queue_words.uncle: a brand-name record (Uncle Ben's), not a food term.
queue_words.debranned: a milling fraction (bran partly removed): not the plain whole flour.
queue_words.malt: malted product: malt forms are parked/unplaced in this project (malt extract PARK); QUEUE.

barley flour or meal.basis: same FDC food ('Barley flour or meal'); one canonical row

long grain rice.basis: grain-length variant of rice; the existing 'rice' row recognises it; one canonical row

pastry flour.basis: grade variant of wheat flour (FDC 'Flour, pastry'); one canonical row (INFERENCE: pastry flour is a wheat flour grade)

semolina flour.basis: FDC 'Flour, semolina' and 'Semolina': one food; one canonical row

refined sorghum flour.basis: grade variant (refined vs whole-grain) of sorghum flour; the existing 'sorghum flour' row recognises it; one canonical row
